analysis: Propranolol is a beta-blocker primarily used for hypertension and anxiety, and it is not commonly associated with depression. While some individuals may experience mood changes, it is not a typical side effect. Oral contraceptives can affect mood due to hormonal fluctuations, and while some users report depressive symptoms, it is not universally experienced. Reserpine is known to deplete monoamines, which can lead to depression, making it likely to cause depressive symptoms. Flupenthixol, an antipsychotic, can also lead to depressive symptoms as a side effect. Given this information, the best-supported option indicating that depression is not a side effect is Propranolol.
